preamble: This image is a real in-engine frame from SANDLINE, a browser first-person shooter set in a desert oil refinery swallowed by a sandstorm; the enemies are armoured combat robots and a giant four-legged walker called COLOSSUS. Produce the target frame of the finished game for the moment described below: the same place and props, the same first-person camera language, rendered as a believable real-time game screenshot (physically based materials, volumetric dust and light, sharp geometry) — not a painting, no brush strokes, no film poster layout. Keep the refinery architecture recognisable from the input.
rules: 16:9 frame. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no user interface unless the moment explicitly asks for it. No human faces. One clear focal point; strong silhouette readability; the only saturated colours are light sources (fire, tracers, robot visors, energy).

directions.name: STORM LOOK
directions.style: Inside the storm the image is nearly monochrome burnt ochre and black: thick blowing sand, shapes reduced to silhouettes at 15 metres, everything further is a gradient. Light sources punch through as hot orange, white-blue lightning and cyan energy. High contrast, graphic, cinematic — the look of a desert storm chase lit from within.

boards.name: SCAN PULSE IN THE STORM
boards.layout: First-person view holding the rifle, deep inside the sandstorm. The player has just fired a scan pulse: a thin bright cyan ring of light is expanding outward across the ground and up the steel structures, like sonar. Where the ring has just passed, surfaces briefly show their glowing wireframe mesh fading back to solid. Three combat robots hidden in the dust are revealed as crisp orange outlined silhouettes with glowing visor slits, at different distances; one is close on the right, raising its weapon. Everything not yet reached by the ring is dark blowing sand.

boards.name: BLAST CLEARS THE AIR
boards.layout: First-person view with the rifle. A grenade has just exploded 12 metres ahead inside the sandstorm: the shockwave has punched a perfectly readable sphere of clear air out of the dust, about 10 metres wide. Inside the sphere everything is suddenly sharp and lit by the orange fireball: two robots are being blown apart, an arm and armour plates spinning away, sparks. The rim of the sphere is a wall of curling compressed dust; outside it the storm is still an opaque ochre murk.

boards.name: IT IS ALREADY COMING
boards.layout: Same dusk yard and first-person rifle as the input, robots fighting in the mid-ground. But the entire horizon behind the refinery is now a sandstorm wall a kilometre tall, towering over the stacks and rolling toward the camera. A lightning flash inside the wall backlights the vast silhouette of a four-legged walking machine, far away and enormous, taller than the flare stack, mid-stride. The dusk sun still rakes the foreground gold; the wall is dark bronze with a blue-white lightning core.

boards.name: THE REFINERY IS THE WEAPON
boards.layout: First-person view with the rifle at night in the storm. A chain reaction is running through the refinery: a ruptured pipe throws a long jet of flame bent sideways by the wind, fire is racing along a pipe rack toward a storage tank that is bulging and splitting with white-hot seams, a steel gantry is buckling. Four robots are caught in it as black silhouettes against the fire, one on fire and falling. Burning embers stream horizontally in the wind; the dust around the fire glows deep orange like a furnace; a lightning bolt strikes the tallest tower in the background.

boards.name: TAKING THE COLOSSUS APART
boards.layout: The giant walker is crippled: its front-left leg has been severed at the knee actuator and lies in the sand trailing sparks, the machine has dropped onto that knee, tilted. Two armour plates have peeled off the hull exposing a glowing blue-white coolant core venting steam. A line of sand in front of it has been fused into glowing orange glass where its beam swept. First-person view from the ground looking up, the player's left hand firing a thin grapple cable that is anchored to the hull, rifle in the right; small robots as silhouettes near its feet for scale. Night, storm, fire light from below, lightning behind.

boards.name: THE HELMET IS THE INTERFACE
boards.layout: First-person view with the rifle inside the storm, seen through a combat helmet visor. This one does include UI: a minimal bold orange-and-bone-white industrial HUD (compass strip at top, segmented shield and health bottom-left, big ammo number bottom-right, objective line top-left) that behaves like a physical display on glass: a crack in the lower-left corner of the visor refracts the HUD, sand grains streak across the glass, a nearby lightning strike makes half the HUD tear and glitch with horizontal slices, and a red 'SHIELD DOWN' strip flashes at the centre top. In the scene a charging robot is three metres away, visor glowing, and a tracer passes the camera.
